newsitem.title: USA: Upheaval in Zaire to go on indefinitely, U.S says.
newsitem.headline: Upheaval in Zaire to go on indefinitely, U.S says.

text.p: The United States said on Monday that it appeared the civil strife in Zaire would continue indefinitely.
"We have an increasing sense that the unrest in Zaire is not going to end anytime soon, that there is a political stalemate," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told a news briefing.

He spoke hours after Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had her second breakfast meeting in a week with visiting South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki whose government is co-hosting with the United Nations peace talks between Zaire's government and rebel groups headed by Laurent Kabila.
The United States is "quite disappointed" that Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko had chosen not to attend peace talks in South Africa, Burns told a news briefing.

"We think the only way that any progress is going to be made in the current civil war in Zaire is for the two protagonists, President Mobutu and Mr. Kabila, to sit down together and hopefully to agree on a ceasefire, and a political way to resolve their problems, not a violent way to do so," he said.

In a speech to a U.S. business summit focusing on Africa, Mbeki took a more optimistic view of the crisis, saying Zaire's people were in a "gripping and epic-making contest (that aims to) give a new birth to their country."

"As Africans, we have a vision, a hope, a prayer about what will come in the end. We see a new Zaire, perhaps with a new name, a Zaire which shall be Democratic, peaceful, prosperous, a defender of human rights and an exemplar of what the new Africa should be, occupying the geographic space that it does at the heart of our Africa," Mbeki said.

"... as Africans, we would like to believe that we know that at the end, what all of us will see, thanks to the wisdom of the people of Zaire themselves, is not the heart of darkness but the light of a new African star," he told the meeting, hosted by the non-profit Coroporate Council on Africa.
